key_insight: Self-evolving agent harnesses can improve an AI system by revising prompts, memory, workflows, and code while keeping model weights fixed, but those revisions must be admitted only through reliable validation.
engineering_relevance: This matters for building maintainable agentic systems because it enables continual adaptation of the software scaffold without retraining the base model, while adding governance for safety and accountability.
method: Formalizes a feedback-driven self-evolution loop for agent harnesses
Separates revision targets from proposal and admission mechanisms
Uses continual PAC-learning analysis to derive generalization, retention, and high-probability admission guarantees
evidence_signal: The paper is primarily theoretical and survey-based, with bounds and admission rules derived under explicit assumptions plus case examples from prior work, rather than a single empirical benchmark study.
watch_item: Persistent harness changes can silently alter behavior over time, so deployment needs fresh independent validation and safeguards when task distributions, evaluators, or privileges change.
